title: Heat with a cosine reaction
plain: In u_t = u_xx + cos(x)u², the reaction averages to zero, but a second-order effect looks like +u³, the borderline Fujita case. Does every positive start blow up?
math: Prove or disprove: for every $0\le u_0\in C_c(\mathbb R)$, $u_0\not\equiv0$, the solution of $u_t=u_{xx}+\cos(x)\,u^2$ on $\mathbb R$ blows up in finite time.
